findings.summary: `m[k] += 1` auto-inserts for Map<Int, Int> but `m[k].push(x)` on a missing key of Map<Int, List<Int>> traps at run time, so I had to write `if d not in at: at[d] = []` first (C++ `at[d].push_back(s)` just works).
findings.evidence: var at: Map<Int, List<Int>> = Map(); at[5].push(1) -> error[R0001]: this key is not in the map; store with `m[k] = v` first

findings.summary: `at.get(d) ?? []` on a Map<Int, List<Int>> copies the whole list (cpl::map_get returns std::optional<std::vector>), and each partition_point call copies it again, so 2285D's 2e5 queries over one 2e5-long list did not finish in 70 s.
findings.evidence: cf2285D.cpp (cpl build --judge codeforces): std::optional<std::vector<ll>> t2 = cpl::map_get(at, d); return t2.has_value() ? *t2 : std::vector<ll>(); ... m5_partition_point(...[&]() -> std::vector<ll> { ...; return ps; }(), ...)

findings.summary: `xs.partition_point(ok)` on a top-level List copies the whole vector into the call every time (generated lambda `return keyed;` by value), making the documented O(log n) search O(n); rewriting as `(0..len).first_true(i => keyed[i] > (d, hi)) ?? len` ran the 2e5x2e5 test in 0.12 s.
findings.evidence: cf2285D.cp variant `keyed.partition_point(p => p > (d, hi))`; cpl build --judge codeforces -> cf2285D.cpp lines 226-227 `D_0_len = ...keyed.size(); return keyed;`; >20 s on n=q=2e5 all-equal input
